question: Which genetic findings explain differences in mosquito bites?
answer: A 2017 study with 23andMe compared the DNA of 16,000 people who rated how much mosquitoes like them. At seven spots in the DNA, a single letter made a difference: at some spots it made people less attractive to mosquitoes, and at others it made them more attractive.
move: Part of your bite risk is written in seven single DNA letters.

web.label: A title asks which genetic findings explain why mosquitoes bite some people more than others. Seven rows, each tappable, compare two groups of people from a 2017 DNA study of 16,000 people rated by how much mosquitoes like them.

source: Veritasium, “Why Mosquitoes Bite Some People More Than Others” (YouTube, 2018)
